sentences.text: This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 102 of 2021, under sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 354, 313, 420 of I.P.C., Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Mahila Thana, District Saharanpur.
Facts in brief are that the informant and applicant Yugank Narula are husband and wife wedded in the year 2019 and applicant Yashik Narula is her Devar.
As per allegation in F.I.R. there was matrimonial dispute between husband and wife.
From the very outset, after the performance of marriage there was harassment on the part of the applicant and other inmates of their family with the informant.
Applicants also threatened the informant to desert and also the mother-in-law took the jewellery of the informant and kept with her.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that in this case both of the applicants are innocent and have committed no offence but on account of mutual dispute between husband and wife present F.I.R. has been lodged against them including their parents also who were granted anticipatory bail by co-ordinate bench of this court.
It is also submitted that the informant and the applicant Yugank Narula were in love affairs which perpetuated in marriage.
Prior to the alleged marriage an F.I.R. was lodged by the informant herself against the applicant which was challenged before this court in writ petition No. 12479 of 2021 and the F.I.R. was quashed.

After marriage when dispute arose a complaint was moved to S.S.P. Ambala on 06.04.2021 in which the facts related to dispute between the husband and wife were narrated in detail but the allegations those are made in the present F.I.R. were lacking which shows that no such incident as mentioned in the present F.I.R. took place between both of them.
No any offence was found to be committed by the applicant Yugank Narula as is apparent from the report submitted by the concerned authority after inquiring into the matter.
It is also submitted that matter was referred to the mediation but could not be settled on account of several reasons.

It is further submitted that there is nothing on record to show that any kind of medicine was administered by the applicants or other members of their family to get the pregnancy terminated except the allegations made by the informant herself in the F.I.R.
It is also submitted that since matter is related to matrimonial dispute, therefore, no purpose will be served by sending them into jail.
It is further submitted that applicant Yashik Narula Devar resides in Bangalore in relation to his job, therefore all the allegations against him are false and frivolous.
Lastly, it is submitted that the applicants are under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicants are released on bail, they would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation, so requested for anticipatory bail.

Learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid and urged that in this case from the very outset intention of the applicant Yugank Narula husband was not good but he always used victim/ informant with bad intention regarding which previous F.I.R.
Yugank Narula vs State Of U.P. on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42337999/
2 was lodged but when he agreed to enter into marriage, the informant also gave her consent and that matter was closed.

sentences.text: Even after marriage he continued to harass the informant.

During the period she was living at Mumbai with him, her harassment continued and later on the applicant Yugank Narula husband left her alone in Mumbai and came at Ambala and she was living there helpless.
In this way, the conduct of the applicant Yugank Narula cannot be said to be in good faith.
It is also urged by learned counsel for the opposite party that during investigation offences are also found to be established.

On considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record and allegations made from both the parties as aforesaid and keeping in view the matter being matrimonial between husband and wife,
possibility of settlement and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case the applicants are entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.

In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicants.
